eligibility_note: Own panel estimation (FE threshold, GMM, GAM); exposure household internet access; 28 European economies (>=10); outcome S80/S20 income inequality (family 4).

sample_corrections.years: 2010-2025 confirmed; unbalanced, 439 obs in harmonized core (448 potential); balanced robustness panel 25 countries/400 obs
sample_corrections.income_groups_covered: no income-group split; all European (EU members plus Iceland), effectively high/upper-middle income only

results.correction: Table 4 values match: high -0.018 to -0.034 (SE 0.012-0.016), significant in Diff L2-L3, Sys L2-L4, Sys L3-L4; low -0.012 to 0.030, none significant. Appendix G two-step: high significant only in Diff L2-L3.
results.quote: GMM partially supports the inequality-reducing mature-diffusion branch but does not fully reproduce the fixed-effects inverted-U pattern.

heterogeneity.correction: Threshold 70.78, LR set 70.45-75.29 correct. Table C2: 2012 low slope 0.018 (0.028), 2013 -0.001 (0.028), 2015-2025 low slope -0.029** (but threshold shifts to 93.42 there).
heterogeneity.quote: Starting the sample in 2012 or 2013 preserves a negative and significant high-access coefficient but removes significance from the positive low-access coefficient.

income_group_note: No income-group comparison; record correctly says not reported.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: too_harsh: authors explicitly disclaim causality and use GMM lags, placebo and Mundlak checks; no causal claim, so moderate rather than serious fits the guide.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: household access share is coarse and saturates near 99%.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: 28 mostly high-income European countries, low regime identified from early years only (Table D1), 28 clusters.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree: estimated threshold, 30 variants plus GMM with imposed threshold; fully reported.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: fragility of low branch and weak GMM disclosed, BH check reported.
risk_of_bias.why: Standard panel with reasonable controls and extensive sensitivity but exogeneity not established; authors hedge as associations.

problems: none; record's 'serious' confounding rating is slightly harsh given non-causal framing. Record's note that only main text was read is superseded: appendices (Tables A1-G2) consistent with record. Record omits the 2-threshold test (p=0.765), linearity bootstrap p=0.032, and GAM average slopes 0.035/-0.032 (minor).
